info.title: toolyard code mode over REST
info.summary: Run a toolyard code-mode script over plain HTTPS: the backup route when MCP fails.
info.description:
An agent whose MCP connection fails can still run a toolyard script with plain HTTPS: `curl` or the `ty` command (`GET /v1/code/ty`). The script runs under the same agent identity, the same policy and the same Inbox approvals as MCP code mode (`executeToolCode`).

## Credentials

All routes except discovery take `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

| Token | Format | Allowed on |
|---|---|---|
| Agent token | `ag_<uuid>.<secret>` | every agent route, including minting session tokens |
| Session token | `tys_<id>.<secret>` | `/v1/code/*`, `GET /v1/agents/approvals/{id}`, `GET /v1/agents/whoami`, `DELETE /v1/agents/session-tokens/{id}` (its own id) |
| Operator token | `tyop_<id>.<secret>` | never on `/v1/code/*` or `/v1/agents/session-tokens*`: 403 |

## HTTP status per run status

Every run route (`POST /v1/code/run`, `GET /v1/code/runs/{id}`, `POST /v1/code/runs/{id}/resume`) answers the run view, with this HTTP status:

| Run status | HTTP |
|---|---|
| `succeeded`, `failed` | 200 |
| `permission_required` | 403 |
| `deferred`, `queued`, `running` (the wait ended first) | 202, with `Location: /v1/code/runs/{id}` |
| `outcome_unknown` | 409 |

Other answers: 400 bad input, 401 no or bad token, 403 operator token or a session token outside its routes, 404 unknown run (or another agent's run), 413 script over 1 MiB, 415 other content types, 422 `idempotency_key_reused` or a resume of a run that is not held, 429 the slot queue is full (with `Retry-After`; no run is created), or a run that waited `queued` for a script slot and got none (`failed`, kind `busy`; nothing ran), 503 the server is restarting or the token could not be checked (with `Retry-After`; no run is created).

## ty exit codes

0 `succeeded`, 1 `failed`, 2 usage or transport error, 3 `permission_required`, 4 `deferred` or still running, 5 busy, 6 `outcome_unknown`.

## Limits

The MCP code-mode limits apply: 5 minutes wall clock, 100 tool calls, 1 MiB output per run, 4 concurrent scripts per server and 3 per agent; a start past either cap is stored `queued` at once and waits up to 30 s for a slot, so `Prefer: wait` (0 included) bounds the answer. Runs and their call records are kept 7 days from their start. A run the server stops (a drain, a shutdown) is `outcome_unknown` with the error kind `interrupted` once it had sent a tool call, and `failed` with kind `interrupted` (nothing ran) before; a run cut off by a process that died is settled the same way after the restart.

post.description:
Agent token only: a session token cannot mint another one, and an operator token is refused. The server never issues a lifetime longer than 3600 seconds. Only the token's SHA-256 is stored, so the token appears in this answer only.

A session token is refused (`401 invalid session token`) when it is expired, revoked, its agent is revoked or blocked, or the parent credential it was minted with is no longer valid (rotated past its grace period, or revoked).

delete.description: Allowed for the parent agent token, or the session token itself. Idempotent: an unknown or already revoked id of the same agent is also 204; another agent's id is 404.

post.description:
Starts a run and answers when it reaches a final or held status, or when the wait ends, whichever is first. The run continues on the server after the response; the client never has to hold the connection.

Body, one of: `text/x-starlark` (the raw script; the reason comes from `X-Toolyard-Reason`, required), or `application/json` (`code`, `reason`, optional `wait_seconds`). The script is at most 1 MiB.

With an `Idempotency-Key`, the same key with the same script and reason returns the existing run in its current state and runs nothing new; the same key with a different script or reason is `422 idempotency_key_reused`.

schema.description: The raw script (UTF-8), at most 1 MiB. Servers are globals: `result = server.tool(param=value)`.

A JavaScript script (UTF-8, also accepted as application/javascript), at most 1 MiB: the body of an async function. `await tools.Server.tool({param: value})`, `tools.call`, `tools.tryCall`, `tools.parallel`, `tools.search`, `console.log`, and `return` the result.

text/javascript.example:
const lib = await tools.context7.resolve_library_id({ libraryName: "react" });
return lib;

example.reason: Find the React docs library id to answer the user's question

get.description: The run view. `Prefer: wait=<seconds>` (0–60, default 0) waits for a final or held status. Only the agent that created the run sees it (with its agent token or any of its session tokens).

post.description:
Resumes a run whose status is `permission_required` or `deferred`, after the owner decided.

- `request_id`: the approved Inbox request that covers the held call. The server reads its grants for this agent and adds `_grant` to each matching call (same tool, parameters within the grant).
- For a `deferred` legacy approval, no body is needed (an empty body or `{}`): the held call resumes with its `approval_id`, also when a `request_id` is given (a grant would run the tool a second time beside the approval's own execution).
- A `permission_required` run needs `request_id` (400 without it), and the request must belong to the agent (400 otherwise). A call no unused grant of the request covers is sent without one, so it is held again (403).

The script runs again from the top, and each call is checked against the call record at its number. A different tool or different arguments, or no record at a number the run reached before, is `failed` with `script_diverged` and nothing more runs. A recorded call that succeeded is answered from the record (`replayed: true`); one that failed after it reached the gateway gets the same failure again (an upstream error may come after a write took effect); a caught `permission_required` call goes again only with a covering grant, else it gets the same hold; a caught `deferred` call is asked again with its own `approval_id`. A recorded call with an unknown outcome stops the resume with `outcome_unknown`; nothing is repeated blindly. A call that is sent waits until every call numbered before it passed its check, and is not sent if one did not. The same `Prefer: wait` and HTTP mapping apply.

409.description: `outcome_unknown` (a run view: a call may have committed upstream; reconcile, never repeat it blindly), or `resume_conflict`: another resume of this run claimed it first, so this one started nothing (`{"error": "resume_conflict", "status": ..., "hint": ...}`); read the run and resume it again if it is still held.

get.description: The same listing as `listToolFiles`: only the tools this agent may see. `?language=javascript` lists the TypeScript stubs (`.d.ts`) instead of the Starlark ones (`.pyi`).
The same stub as `readToolFile`. Unknown files, and tools this agent may not see, are 404.

The tool's `Input` and `Output` types and its `Call` signature, generated from its input and output schemas, for JavaScript scripts. `/v1/code/files/{server}.d.ts` is one server's tools, and `/v1/code/files/index.d.ts` declares the `tools` object, its helpers (`call`, `tryCall`, `parallel`, `search`) and `console`. Unknown files, and tools this agent may not see, are 404.

The same search as the `tools.search` tool, over the tools this agent may use. `mode=keyword` (default) ranks by BM25 over tool names, descriptions, parameter names and parameter descriptions; `mode=regex` matches an RE2 pattern of at most 200 characters, case-insensitive unless the pattern turns that off; `auto` is keyword; `semantic` answers 400 unless the server configured it. `detail` is `name`, `summary` (default) or `full` (with the input and output schemas).

get.description: The same text as `getToolDocs`. Unknown tools, and tools this agent may not see, are 404.
One Python 3 file, standard library only. Save it, `chmod +x` it, set `TOOLYARD_URL` and `TOOLYARD_TOKEN_FILE`, and run `ty --help`.

agentToken.description: An agent token. Allowed on every agent route, including minting session tokens.

sessionToken.description: A session token for one agent session (T3 writes it to TOOLYARD_TOKEN_FILE). Allowed on /v1/code/*, GET /v1/agents/approvals/{id}, GET /v1/agents/whoami and DELETE /v1/agents/session-tokens/{id} for its own id.

RunID.name: id
RunID.description: The run id from the run view.

Server.name: server
Server.description: The server identifier as `listToolFiles` shows it.

Tool.name: tool
Tool.description: The tool identifier as `listToolFiles` shows it.

PreferWait.name: Prefer
PreferWait.description: `wait=<seconds>`, 0–60: default 25 on `POST /v1/code/run` (`wait_seconds` in a JSON body wins) and on a resume, 0 on `GET`. A larger value counts as 60. The server answers when the run reaches a final or held status, or when the wait ends, whichever is first.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: 1–128 printable ASCII characters, scoped to the agent. The same key with the same script and reason returns the existing run and runs nothing new; with a different script or reason it is `422 idempotency_key_reused`.

ToolyardReason.name: X-Toolyard-Reason
ToolyardReason.description: Why the script runs, for the audit record. Required with `Content-Type: text/x-starlark`; a JSON body carries `reason` instead.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

RunFinished.description: `succeeded` or `failed`: the run reached a final status.

RunPending.description: `deferred` (a legacy approval is pending), or `queued` or `running` (the wait ended first). The run continues on the server; read the `Location` with `Prefer: wait`.

RunHeld.description: `permission_required`: a call needs the owner's approval and the run view's `held` names it; submit `held.draft` as an Inbox request, then resume with its `request_id`. An operator token, or a session token outside its routes, gets an Error instead.

RunOutcomeUnknown.description: `outcome_unknown`: a call may have committed upstream. Reconcile its state; never repeat it blindly.

Unauthorized.description: No token, or a bad, expired or revoked one.

Forbidden.description: An operator token, or a session token outside its routes.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: A content type other than text/x-starlark or application/json.

Unprocessable.description: `idempotency_key_reused` (the key was used with a different script or reason), or `run_not_held`: a resume of a run that is not held (the body then carries the run's `status`).

Busy.description: Code mode is busy. Either the slot queue is full (twice the per-agent cap for one agent, four times the global cap in all): no run is created. Or the body is a run view of a run that waited `queued` up to 30 seconds (`-codemode-queue-wait`) for a script slot and got none: `failed` with kind `busy`, nothing ran, and its Idempotency-Key is free again. Try again after `Retry-After` seconds.

Unavailable.description: The server is restarting, or the token could not be checked. Nothing was started; try again after `Retry-After` seconds.

session_id.description: 1–128 printable ASCII characters. It becomes the verified client session id in the audit of every call made with the token.

ttl_seconds.description: Lifetime in seconds. The server never issues a longer one.

token.description: `tys_<id>.<secret>`. Write it to a file only you can read; never print or log it.

reason.description: Why the script runs, for the audit record.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for a final or held status. Wins over `Prefer: wait`.

request_id.description: The approved Inbox request that covers the held call. Omit it for a `deferred` legacy approval.

RunError.description: Set when the run is `failed` or `outcome_unknown`.

kind.description: Kinds include script_error, tool_error, timeout (the run's own clock), limit, script_diverged, grant_invalid, busy (no script slot came free; nothing ran), outcome_unknown, internal and interrupted (the server stopped the run: failed with it when no tool call had been sent, outcome_unknown once one had).

replayed.description: True when a resume answered the call from the call record instead of sending it upstream again.

ms.description: How long the call took in milliseconds; 0 until it finished.

matched.description: Tools that matched, before the limit.

code.description: The name a script calls it by: tools.<code> in JavaScript, <code>(...) in Starlark.

Held.description: Set when the run is `permission_required` or `deferred`: the call that stopped it.

draft.description: The Inbox request draft the gateway returned. Complete it and submit it (from code, toolyard.inbox_request), then resume with the request id.

approval_id.description: Set for a legacy deferred approval; resume with no body after the owner decided.

message.description: The gateway's text for the call: what to do next.

run_id.description: Also the run_id of every audit row of the run.

result.description: The JSON value the script assigned to `result`; null when none.

logs.description: print() output, one entry per line.

error.description: A short message, or a code such as idempotency_key_reused.
